A one-page map of the three stage notebooks: what data each one makes, which models it fits, and how the checks carry through. Use it to see where we are and why the next notebook exists.

## The arc

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S1["<b>Stage 1</b><br/>Real Q2 data<br/>mod0 vs mod2"]
  S2["<b>Stage 2</b><br/>Simulate from mod2<br/>iid site effects, nothing spatial"]
  S3a["<b>Stage 3, part 1</b><br/>+ nonlinear TreePerimeter<br/>a smooth (GAM)"]
  S3b["<b>Stage 3, part 2</b><br/>+ spatial field<br/>Hefley's models"]
  S1 -- "fitted values become the truth<br/>(results/stage1.rds)" --> S2
  S2 -- "swap the line for a curve" --> S3a
  S3a -- "add a field that depends<br/>on where a tree is" --> S3b
```

Each stage keeps the previous stage's truth and adds one thing. The questions at every stage are the same: **do the checks see the problem**, and **do the estimates come out right** (bias, coverage)?

## One pass through a stage

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  T["Truth<br/>(β, σ, φ, curve, field)"] --> SIM["Simulate one<br/>data set<br/>(48 rows, 24 trees)"]
  SIM --> FIT["Fit every model<br/>flavor"]
  FIT --> CHK["Checks<br/>within a tree: by-tree residuals, partner correlation<br/>between trees: map, lineup, Moran's I"]
  FIT --> EST["Estimates<br/>vs the truth"]
  CHK --> REP{"Repeat 200–250×<br/>at each ramp level"}
  EST --> REP
  REP --> OUT["Rejection rate · bias · 95% CI coverage"]
```

## The data-generating processes

All three simulations share one skeleton. A stage only changes what goes into the linear predictor η:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph eta["log μ = η  (one row per tree × aspect)"]
    direction TB
    B0["Intercept"]
    TP["TreePerimeter<br/><i>stage 2: straight line β·x</i><br/><i>stage 3: hump peaking at 15 m</i>"]
    AS["Aspect (e / s)"]
    DR["DistReef (m)"]
    A["Site effect a_j ~ N(0, σ²)<br/>iid: one per tree, shared by its two rows<br/><i>stage 2 ramp: σ = 0 … 1.6</i>"]
    W["Spatial field w = broad + medium + fine layers<br/>(ranges 600 / 200 / 60 m), total SD 1<br/>nearby trees get similar values<br/><i>stage 3 part 2 only; complexity = how the variance is split across layers</i>"]
  end
  eta --> MU["μ = exp(η)"]
  MU --> Y["Abundance ~ NB1(μ)<br/>Var = μ (1 + φ)"]
```

| | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3, part 1 | Stage 3, part 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data | real | simulated | simulated | simulated |
| TreePerimeter | line | line | **hump** | hump |
| Site effect a_j (iid) | (estimated) | **σ ramped** | σ from stage 1 | σ from stage 1 |
| Spatial field w | — | — | — | **variance moved to finer layers** |
| Code | — | `sim_glmm()` | `sim_nonlinear()` | `sim_spatial()` |

## The models

Every model is NB1 in glmmTMB. Model flavors keep the same colour in every notebook (`sim/model_compare.R`).

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph st12["Stages 1 and 2"]
    M0["<b>No location</b> (mod0)<br/>TreePerimeter + Aspect + DistReef"]
    M2["<b>Location RE</b> (mod2)<br/>… + (1 | LocationID)"]
    M0 -- "add the iid site term" --> M2
  end
  subgraph st3a["Stage 3, part 1"]
    L["<b>Location RE</b><br/>straight line in TreePerimeter"]
    G["<b>GAM</b><br/>s(TreePerimeter) + Aspect + DistReef<br/>+ (1 | LocationID)"]
    L -- "line → smooth" --> G
  end
  subgraph st3b["Stage 3, part 2: GAM + one spatial term"]
    G0["<b>GAM</b><br/>ignores space"]
    SXY["<b>GAM + s(x, y)</b><br/>spline surface"]
    FC["<b>Full covariance</b><br/>exp(pos + 0 | grp)"]
    EB["<b>Eigen basis</b><br/>5 eigenvectors of R(200 m)"]
    KB["<b>Knot basis</b><br/>6 Gaussian kernels"]
    G0 --> SXY
    G0 --> FC
    G0 --> EB
    G0 --> KB
  end
  M2 --> L
  G --> G0
```

## Hefley's idea: two places to put space

Space can go in the **mean** as basis functions, or in the **variance** as a correlation matrix. If the basis coefficients are random, α ~ N(0, σ²I), the two are the same model, because Zα has covariance σ²ZZ′.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph mean["In the mean (first-order)"]
    direction TB
    Zm["log μ = Xβ + Zα<br/>columns of Z = surfaces over the map"]
  end
  subgraph var["In the variance (second-order)"]
    direction TB
    Vm["log μ = Xβ + η<br/>η ~ N(0, σ² R(ϕ))<br/>R = correlation between every pair of sites"]
  end
  Zm <-->|"α ~ N(0, σ²I)  ⇒  Cov(Zα) = σ² ZZ′<br/>R = QΛQ′  ⇒  Z = QΛ^½ gives ZZ′ = R"| Vm
```

The three spatial models in stage 3 are steps along a single trade-off between exactness and cost:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  FC["<b>Full covariance</b><br/>n × n matrix R(ϕ), ϕ estimated<br/>exact, but cost grows like n³"]
  EB["<b>Eigen basis</b><br/>keep the m leading eigenvectors<br/>Z = Q_m Λ_m^½ (24 × 5)<br/>ϕ fixed at 200 m"]
  KB["<b>Knot basis</b><br/>Gaussian bump at each of k knots<br/>Z = kernel weights (24 × 6)<br/>local support, no n × n matrix at all"]
  SXY["<b>s(x, y)</b><br/>spline basis + penalty<br/>(the GAM version of the same idea)"]
  FC -- "reduced rank" --> EB
  EB -- "skip the matrix:<br/>build Z directly" --> KB
  KB -. "same machinery as" .-> SXY
```

The same "basis + penalty / random coefficients" idea is behind `s(TreePerimeter)` in part 1. That's why stage 3 starts with a one-dimensional smooth before it moves to a smooth over the map.

## The checks: are the residuals independent?

Every model here assumes each count's residual is independent of every other's. The design gives that assumption two ways to fail, and there is one check (plus a picture) for each:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  IID["Assumption: residuals are independent"]
  IID --> W["<b>Within a tree</b><br/>the east and south counts<br/>share something unmodelled"]
  IID --> B["<b>Between trees</b><br/>nearby trees share<br/>something unmodelled"]
  W --> WP["Picture: residuals by tree<br/>(authors' boxplot, by LocationID)"]
  W --> WT["Test: partner correlation<br/>cor(east, south residual)<br/>vs 999 shuffled pairings"]
  B --> BP["Pictures: residual map,<br/>lineup of 9 maps"]
  B --> BT["Test: Moran's I<br/>4 nearest neighbours<br/>vs 999 shuffled maps"]
  WT -.->|"what an omitted site effect<br/>creates (stage 2)"| S2["Stage 2"]
  BT -.->|"what a spatial field<br/>creates (stage 3, part 2)"| S3["Stage 3, part 2"]
```

Both tests use the same logic: compute a correlation with a "neighbour" (the other count at the same tree, or the nearest trees), then shuffle who the neighbours are to see what that correlation looks like when it is meaningless.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  R["Pearson residuals<br/>(one per row, 48)"] --> PR["East vs south<br/>per tree (24 pairs)"]
  PR --> PT["Partner correlation"]
  R --> LM["Mean per tree<br/>(24 values)"]
  LM --> MAP["Map"]
  LM --> MI["Moran's I"]
  RE["Location intercepts"] --> LU["Lineup"]
  C["Coefficients ± 95% CI"] --> TR["vs the true β:<br/>bias and coverage"]
```
